name: Two shelves from one immutable ledger
hypothesis: Can ordinary code preserve every received fragment while showing the best-supported answer separately from same-case alternatives?
inputs: the frozen source cards and their sender-declared tags
build_rules: Copy all 480 received fragments into an append-only ledger before making a view.
USED is exactly the set selected by Gate 15D.

SAME_CASE contains an unselected fragment only when its frozen sender card and task contract agree: lookalike for a condition-mismatch task or dependent-copy for a copied-report dispute, and the question's named object occurs in the fragment.
CONDITIONAL is a badge on selected safe-action or source-checking fragments; it does not remove them from USED.
All remaining fragments are OTHER: hidden by default, never deleted.
Fragments with one lineage are one visible dependent view, but every original record remains in the ledger.
anti_leak_rule: Expected answers, required_sources, distractor_sources and Gate 15C/15D gold labels may be used only after construction to score the frozen result; they may not choose a shelf.
boundaries: This reuses the same synthetic English questions seen in Gates 15C and 15D.
Sender-declared tags are trusted in this mechanics test.
It tests storage and views, not whether unseen senders label capsules honestly.
It does not test the final natural-language writer.
